title: 1975 AHSME Problem 3
statement:
Which of the following inequalities are satisfied for all real numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z\) which satisfy \(x\lt a,\) \(y\lt b,\) and \(z\lt c?\)

I. \(xy+yz+zx\lt ab+bc+ca\)

II. \(x^2+y^2+z^2\lt a^2+b^2+c^2\)

III. \(xyz\lt abc\)

solutions.text:
Take \(a=b=1,\ c=-1,\) and \(x=y=0,\ z=-10.\) The required three coordinate inequalities hold. But I becomes \(0\lt-1,\) II becomes \(100\lt3,\) and III becomes \(0\lt-1,\) all false. Thus none is universally true.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The variables are real, so increasing a number need not increase its square or its products
